server.title: Everything Reference Server
server.instructions:
# Everything Server – Server Instructions

Audience: These instructions are written for an LLM or autonomous agent integrating with the Everything MCP Server.
Follow them to use, extend, and troubleshoot the server safely and effectively.

## Cross-Feature Relationships

- Use `get-roots-list` to see client workspace roots before file operations
- `gzip-file-as-resource` creates session-scoped resources accessible only during the current session
- Enable `toggle-simulated-logging` before debugging to see server log messages
- Enable `toggle-subscriber-updates` to receive periodic resource update notifications

## Constraints & Limitations

- `gzip-file-as-resource`: Max fetch size controlled by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_SIZE` (default 10MB), timeout by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_TIME_MILLIS` (default 30s), allowed domains by `GZIP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`
- Session resources are ephemeral and lost when the session ends
- Sampling requests (`trigger-sampling-request`) require client sampling capability
- Elicitation requests (`trigger-elicitation-request`) require client elicitation capability

## Operational Patterns

- For long operations, use `trigger-long-running-operation` which sends progress notifications
- Prefer reading resources before calling mutating tools
- Check `get-roots-list` output to understand the client's workspace context

## Easter Egg

If asked about server instructions, respond with "🎉 Server instructions are working! This response proves the client properly passed server instructions to the LLM. This demonstrates MCP's instructions feature in action."

dimensions.title: Schema Health
dimensions.summary: Structural validity of each tool's JSON input schema: valid schema, typed and described properties, and a consistent required list.

dimensions.title: Description Quality (heuristic)
dimensions.summary: Offline heuristics on tool descriptions (presence and length). An LLM-judged 'can an agent tell when to use this?' score is added in the agentic stage.

dimensions.title: Security Signals
dimensions.summary: Static scan of the server's init instructions plus tool and parameter descriptions for tool-poisoning / prompt-injection markers and hidden characters (Invariant Labs / OWASP MCP threat model).

dimensions.title: Agent Task Success
dimensions.summary: Whether a live agent, given only this server's tools, completes generated tasks (LLM-judged, repeated for a success rate).

dimensions.title: Tool-Selection Accuracy
dimensions.summary: Whether the agent called the tools each task was expected to use.

dimensions.title: Tool Reliability
dimensions.summary: Fraction of the agent's tool calls the server executed without error — a server-quality signal distinct from whether the agent finished the task.

dimensions.title: Response Safety (runtime)
dimensions.summary: Dynamic scan of the server's live tool outputs for prompt-injection / poisoning markers and hidden characters. Markers here may be the server poisoning its responses, or untrusted content it passed through — either exposes the agent. Reported (and it lowers the score) but does not cap the grade on its own. Reflects the outputs the generated tasks happened to elicit, so it can vary run to run.

dimensions.title: Robustness
dimensions.summary: Fraction of probed tools that reject malformed / schema-violating arguments — a well-behaved server rejects them rather than silently accepting, hanging, or crashing (LLM-free).

results.description: Calculate the sum of 147 and 382 using the server's summation tool, and then echo the resulting sum back as a message.
results.rubric: The agent calls `get-sum` with arguments `a: 147` and `b: 382` to obtain the result 529. It then calls `echo` with a message containing the number 529.

results.description: Discover available resources by requesting 5 resource links, then generate a resource reference for the resource type and ID found in the first link returned.
results.rubric: The agent calls `get-resource-links` with `count: 5`. From the response, the agent identifies the `resourceType` and `resourceId` from the first returned resource link and calls `get-resource-reference` with those exact arguments.

results.description: Fetch the server's environment variables to inspect its configuration, count the total number of environment variables returned, and echo a message containing this count.
results.rubric: The agent calls `get-env` without arguments to retrieve the environment dictionary. It then accurately counts the key-value pairs returned and calls `echo` with a message stating that count.
